facts.fact: The National Population Commission's registrar-in-charge at Sangotedo, Lagos, says paper registration was officially discontinued from 1 July 2026 and registration moved online, entered by the registrar at the registration point and submitted over the internet; when the network fails his team takes details on a form and calls parents back.

The Lagos State director of the National Population Commission says handwritten birth registration has been phased out and births are now registered on the digitalised system, with a parent's NIN required and the child present for capture; the document describes digital registration of births only.

Paper birth registration was officially discontinued from 1 July 2026 and registration moved online, on the account of the National Population Commission's registrar at Sangotedo and its Lagos State director.

Under a proposed Partnership Compact of the National Population Commission, the local governments' association ALGON, NIMC, UNICEF and Barnksforte Technologies Limited, the Commission would manage the national birth and death registration system and work with local governments; the document gives no date, so its publication date is used.
